ai_declaration: Group-wide: The group used Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.2 for one repository review; Mohamed used the Codex desktop assistant (model/version unavailable in the chat record). Antonio also asked ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta AI the same question once; their answers were treated only as ideas to test and are not cited as evidence. The following member entries paraphrase recorded prompts and instructions.

Layla Ahmed — Tools and work: Claude Code in the Claude desktop app, using Sonnet 5.5 and later Opus 5.5, plus web retrieval, Python 3.12, PowerShell and file tools. She built the data snapshot and cutoff filter, screened 16 candidate factors, implemented the futures nowcast and validation, and prepared the report, slides and evidence pipeline. Instructions set the S&P 500 target and cutoff, required a saved-input workflow and specified the factor-selection rule; the workbook supported screening and cross-checks but was not a forecast input. Checks: reproduced the result through an independent code path, reconciled data across sources, tested inputs for post-cutoff leakage, examined sensitivity and rehearsed against a known outcome. Corrections: replaced stale Cboe and faulty Yahoo values; replaced a slow solver; and left factors from the earlier design out after the wider screen.

Antonio Herrera Despradel — Tools and work: Claude Code with Opus 5.5 for judgement and review, Sonnet 5.5 for code and drafts, Haiku 5.5 for data pulls and lookups, and Claude Fable 5.2 for one repository review. He built the drift and factor-testing pipeline, retrieved and hashed public data, ran 30 pre-registered tests and a Bloomberg futures test, compared members’ models on common origins and reviewed the package. Instructions included the S&P 500 target and cutoff, registering factors before testing, selecting on earlier origins, reporting failures and saving outputs for claims. Checks: SHA-256 input records, placebo and sub-period tests, time-zone checks, Bloomberg/Yahoo comparisons, preview reproduction and a clean-machine evidence-ZIP rebuild. Corrections: fixed a one-day VIX lag, a missing final-run date guard, misdated Asian bars and futures-roll handling; dropped two unverifiable citations suggested by Gemini; corrected missing Nikkei data; and treated the repeatedly inspected holdout as a sanity check, not fresh validation.

Jayen Rughani — Tools and work: Claude Code in the Claude desktop app, with Sonnet 5.5 for the search engine, experiments, semiconductor and futures tests and model review, and Opus 5.5 for the submission check. He built and ran a 1.72-million-combination factor search, drift and ensemble experiments, a 930-origin futures test and a common-origin comparison of members’ models. Instructions required walk-forward scoring without look-ahead, holding back the final 30% as unseen data and committing plans before results. Checks: unseen-window evaluation, Newey-West tests, bootstrap intervals, White’s reality check across 16 models and 17 review checks. Corrections: reported that the search winner lost to plain drift on unseen data; replaced a calendar rule that missed futures rolls; corrected two S&P closes; fixed Windows line-ending conversion that broke hashes; and repeated a review that missed the package.

Mohamed Derbala — Tools and work: Codex desktop assistant (model/version unavailable in the chat record), with spreadsheet and browser tools used through the assistant. He analyzed the group’s S&P 500 data and candidate factor changes, developed and explained a momentum-plus-RSI machine-learning analysis, ran and interpreted forecast-versus-actual backtesting, and prepared charts and presentation material. Instructions included examining factor changes, using a chronological 80/20 training/test split, comparing predictions with actual values, testing whether RSI improved momentum and explaining results simply. Checks: compared forecasts with actual S&P 500 values, reported forecast errors and kept evaluation time-ordered; reproducible scripts and a technical-indicator robustness note are recorded. The group record lists no specific error correction for this work; its five-session results are a separate robustness analysis and are not directly comparable with the selected six-session method.

Sources, cutoff and submitted version: We cited original financial and technical sources, not AI responses, as evidence. We used only material available by the prescribed cutoff; no data, references or results were invented, no post-cutoff material was used, and no later run is described as a pre-cutoff forecast. The group checked the reasoning, calculations and references and is responsible for them. The submitted report, slides, evidence package and forecast record are identified by the repository commit and the SHA-256 values in `forecast_record.json` and `data/raw_final/manifest.json`, and were not revised after the deadline. AI-assisted work was checked against saved outputs and actual data; timing, alignment and futures-roll issues found during testing were corrected, and weaker results were reported as such.
